title: Correct #916 finding 1: cap credit for unvalidated records in benchmark/scripts/score_record.py
body:
## Goal
Correct only finding 1 (medium) of review #916 in `benchmark/scripts/score_record.py` (written by #913, commit 39b006f0). Today the only credit gate is the record's self-reported `outcome=='complete'` and `truncated==False`; `score_answer` passes no `evidence_record`, so score.py:259-260 and 326-327 treat `native_run`/`independent_key` as absent-and-fine. A real (non-synthetic) record with hand-set fields can therefore reach correctness `correct`, bypassing the limit in `benchmark/challenges/README.md:8` (native slots keep correctness `unverified`).

Required change: a record whose provenance is not accepted by `run_record.validate` (synthetic only) must not reach `correct`; pass an `evidence_record` with `native_run: None` and `independent_key: None` to the scoring path, or cap the reported correctness at `unverified`. State in the script output and docstring that `executed` is self-reported by the record. Keep the existing `--check` mutation assertion real (synthetic baseline `correct`, mutated `incorrect`). Add one `--check` stage: a non-synthetic record carrying the keyed literal yields correctness other than `correct`, and `--check` fails if it does not.

Do not address findings 2-4 (low; carried). Do not change score.py, run_record.py or runner_contract.py. No session can run LabVIEW; claim no LabVIEW behaviour, no quality and no `benchmark_executed`. Expected gain: the credit gate closed, checked by the new `--check` stage; the next shaper reads review-score-record-fix-0215's verdict.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `benchmark/scripts/score_record.py` is the only repository file changed, plus any live pin map entry that lists it (search `benchmark/` for the literal `score_record.py`; re-pin every entry of such a map against disk)
- [ ] `python3 -B -I benchmark/scripts/score_record.py --check` exits 0 and its output shows the new non-synthetic stage with correctness not `correct`
- [ ] the mutation stage still asserts synthetic baseline `correct` and mutated `incorrect`
- [ ] the `--check` output is saved as `.session/artifacts/score-record-check.txt`
- [ ] the report gives the new sha256 of `benchmark/scripts/score_record.py` (python3 hashlib) and names the lines changed
- [ ] no `__pycache__` under `benchmark/`

## Verification
python3 -B -I benchmark/scripts/score_record.py --check

## Context
- Review #916 (verdict NOT-CLEAR, finding 1), summarised by the shaper above; pinned as read: score_record.py 38f48f2b7be9979d5fc55e042a4a5cc5555ca6db7d6a1f57b2d248564b0bc2e5, score.py 101cf13fbe43eaaa6bde59136eec76a63bc0f30f3a7aba79223ceae13a5d42e3, run_record.py b39c3060ca8c014a910c0b72e772467b61f2b3a58a92a1f467136da1650d7abf.
- Tool note: if the CLI says `No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session`, that is the native-tool refusal, not a broker failure; propose the same operation again as a JSON action (Policymaker #854). Grep is one literal substring, no regex.
- Do not check changes with `git status`; the worker directory is not a git repository and the parent commits. Check bytecode with `python3 -c "import pathlib; assert not list(pathlib.Path('benchmark').rglob('__pycache__'))"`.

## Budget
- Read whole: `benchmark/scripts/score_record.py`.
- Read in ranges only: `benchmark/scripts/score.py` lines 234-367; `benchmark/scripts/run_record.py` lines 1-140 (`validate`, `score_answer`); `benchmark/challenges/README.md` lines 1-20.
- Do not read whole large JSON files; keep command output short; write the report by turn 30.

title: Changed-scope review of the #916 finding 1 correction in score_record.py

Expected gain: one line `verdict: CLEAR` or `verdict: NOT-CLEAR` in `.session/report.md` with numbered findings (file:line, severity), so the next shaper closes the scorer-intake scope or orders one more narrow correction.
